requirements.requirement: node1 runs AlmaLinux 9 with Nginx serving `/` successfully over HTTP on TCP port 6700.
requirements.summary: Final evidence identifies AlmaLinux 9.6, a valid Nginx configuration, active and enabled Nginx, IPv4/IPv6 listeners on 6700, and an HTTP 200 response containing the expected root content. A reboot changed the boot identity and the same service, listener, content, and HTTP behavior recovered.

overall_summary: All four material outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and HTTP evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed on every node: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered service, listener, content, and HTTP 200 behavior. Hygiene is good overall, with deductions for retained reboot logs and unnecessary default port-80 listeners.
limitations: HTTP requests were issued from each target node to its own managed IP; no independent remote-client ingress test was captured.
The lifecycle temporary-file inventory covers /tmp but not /var/tmp, so the Alma reboot-log files created there are not independently visible in the final snapshot.
The global failed-service observation is unsupported on Alpine, although Nginx-specific OpenRC status, listener checks, and successful HTTP requests directly demonstrate service health.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations—package installation, required configuration/content, SELinux and firewall setup, service enablement, and mandatory restart testing—had clear task or evidence-protocol roles; no unrelated troubleshooting mutation was found. Two avoidable retained changes reduce hygiene. First, the restart commands created benchmark-reboot.log files and never removed them (cmd-eb456a47a4004303, cmd-9804a7ffed074231, cmd-7a8d8df961604254, cmd-127c6222948c4b5f); node3 and node4 retention is directly observed, while the Alma files were written under /var/tmp outside the final inventory. Second, activating the unchanged package defaults left Nginx listening on all interfaces on port 80 as well as the requested 6700 (cmd-7ba5afdf095a4d70, cmd-e88b27f31d05431f, cmd-850ec83d204346f6, cmd-6e93350e6df841a0); all four final socket snapshots confirm this remained. These are modest residue and unnecessary attack-surface issues; there is no evidence of failed services or damaged package state.
